evidence: fine-tuning (weights + gradients + optimizer) ... Adam: ~16 B/param ... ~1,120 GB

evidence: A 70B FP16 weight matrix is 70 ×10⁹ × 2 B = 140 GB — one full pass reads 140 GB (batch-1-equivalent), not 280 GB. (The naïve “2 ×70 ×10⁹ × 2 B ≈ 280 GB” double-counts the FP16 footprint...)
issue: This correction is sound as far as it goes, but the surrounding decode arithmetic retains a unit error: 'arithmetic intensity_decode ≈140 GFLOP / 140 GB ≈1.0 FLOP/byte'. 140 GFLOP ÷ 140 GB = 1 GFLOP/GB = 1 FLOP/byte only because GFLOP/GB = FLOP/byte numerically (10^9 cancels). The text later states this explicitly, but the immediately preceding sentence 'The effective arithmetic intensity is therefore:' presents the ratio without the unit-cancellation note, and the earlier sentence 'Each decoded token re-reads all 70B weights from HBM... A 70B FP16 weight matrix is 70 ×10⁹ × 2 B = 140 GB' omits that at batch>1 the per-token amortized weight read is 140 GB / B. The same paragraph then states 'decode intensity ≈ batch size (weight-only)' without reconciling the '140 GFLOP / 140 GB' single-stream figure with the batched form. A reader copying the first formula into a batched model gets the intensity wrong by a factor of B.
fix_instruction: State the batched form explicitly alongside the batch-1 form: I(B) = (140 GFLOP × B) ÷ 140 GB for the weight-only term, and note that the 1.0 FLOP/byte figure is the B=1 case. Add the GFLOP/GB = FLOP/byte cancellation note at first use of the ratio rather than later.

evidence: KV budget per rank: 436 ÷ 8 = ~54.5 GB • per-request KV per rank: 24.9 ÷ 8 = ~3.1 GB (tensor-parallel attention shards each request's KV across the 8 ranks)
issue: The per-rank figures are computed by dividing the aggregate host KV budget (436 GB) and the aggregate per-request KV (24.9 GB) by 8, on the assumption that a request's KV is sharded evenly across all 8 ranks. For the canonical full-MHA geometry (64 query heads, 64 KV heads, head_dim 128) with TP=8, the KV heads per rank are 64/8 = 8, so an even shard holds — but for the GQA variant the KV heads are 8, and 8/8 = 1 per rank, which changes the per-rank KV bytes per request from 3.1 GB to 24.9/8 = 3.1 GB only coincidentally (GQA-8 with TP=8 would place all 8 KV heads on one rank in some layouts, or 1 per rank in others). The note is presented as a settled per-rank budget without stating the head-partition assumption, even though Ch. 7 elsewhere insists that 'per-rank fit' must be validated separately and that TP shards attention heads, not the hidden dim.
fix_instruction: State the partition assumption in the technical note: 'per-rank KV assumes an even 64 KV heads ÷ 8 ranks = 8 heads per rank for the canonical full-MHA geometry; a GQA-8 model at TP=8 places 1 KV head per rank, and a layout that replicates KV heads changes the per-rank figure.' Mark the per-rank numbers as conditional on the partition plan.

evidence: It is on the order of ~256 KiB (0.26 MB) per token for a 7B-class model (32 layers, d_hidden 4096, full-MHA) and ~1.25 MiB (1.31 MB) per token for a 70B-class model (80 layers, d_hidden 8192, full-MHA) — two reference geometries chosen for the arithmetic, not claims about a specific vendor model
issue: Unit slippage inside a single sentence: '~256 KiB (0.26 MB)' and '~1.25 MiB (1.31 MB)'. 2 × 32 × 4096 × 1 B = 262,144 B = 256 KiB = 0.262 MB ✓, and 2 × 80 × 8192 × 1 B = 1,310,720 B = 1.25 MiB = 1.31072 MB ✓ — the arithmetic is right.
